name: Nourish & Co. Kitchen Service Uniform Set
description:
The standard uniform for kitchen workers at Nourish & Co. contracted canteens — the corporate cafeteria chains that feed the working population of GLMZ's Tier 2 and 3 commercial zones. The set includes a double-breasted chef coat in heat-resistant spun polyaramid, a bib apron with a wipe-clean surface coating, and adjustable trouser pulls. The coat is rated for sustained heat up to 260°C and resists oil, acid, and most cleaning chemical splashes. Color is white with Nourish & Co.'s green-stripe trim. The apron has an embedded RFID tag that logs when it's collected and returned from the facility's laundry system — a measure ostensibly for inventory control.

The uniform is produced in configurations that address the full range of kitchen workers in 2200: the coat collar includes a snap-out panel for workers with neck-mounted chrome or BCI hardware, and alternative headgear options include structured caps with horn-clearance inserts and elasticized wraps that conform to ear modifications or unusual head shapes. The standard hairnet alternative for workers with bioluminescent or modified skin is a full-coverage food-safe skull cap. The uniform is the property of the facility, not the worker, and must be returned at end of employment — a fact enforced by the RFID logging system.
cultural_context: Kitchen work in M88 is grueling, essential, and chronically undervalued. The Nourish & Co. uniform marks you as part of the invisible infrastructure that feeds the city. Workers develop strong bonds with their kitchen crews — the uniform is shared, the work is shared, and the complaints about the RFID tracking are universal.
story_hooks: The RFID logging system in a Nourish & Co. canteen has been cross-referencing uniform collection times with worker political association data — someone is using the laundry system as a surveillance tool.
A kitchen worker discovers that her facility's food supply chain runs through a Crucible subsidiary that's been substituting synthetic protein sources without disclosure.
A Tier 4 corporate dining facility that uses Nourish & Co. contract staff has a contamination incident — and the kitchen workers are being pressured to sign NDAs before anyone investigates.
